key_insight: In entropy variables, the nonlinear entropy-stable extension of Navier–Stokes–Fourier forms a fourth-order quasi-cubic system whose quasi-linear approximation preserves entropy stability and the highest-order derivative terms.
engineering_relevance: The closure offers a continuum-model route to improved rarefied-gas heat-transfer predictions beyond standard Navier–Stokes–Fourier.
method: Derive the entropy-variable formulation using an inverse collision-operator derivative identity.
Apply the quasi-linear approximation to stationary heat transfer between parallel plates.
Analyze plane-wave dispersion using the one-dimensional linearized equations.
evidence_signal: For parallel-plate heat transfer, interpolated boundary conditions yield closer agreement with DSMC temperature profiles and Sherman–Lees heat flux than Navier–Stokes–Fourier, while the linearized dispersion analysis finds all frequency modes stable.
watch_item: The reported heat-transfer gains depend on boundary-condition specification, and the abstract does not establish performance for multidimensional or turbulent flows.
paper_title: Extensions to the Navier-Stokes-Fourier Equations for Rarefied Transport: Entropy Variable Formulation, Heat Transfer and Dispersion of a Non-Linear Entropy Stable Closure
